intent: To explain the concept of progressive taxation where tax rates increase as income levels rise.

requirements.question: Must the video show the full monotonic sequence, or only the endpoint comparison?
Should the video quantify the gap/ratio between richest and poorest, or only say rich people pay more?
Is the top-end value 21.000 or 0.7000 required, or is it enough that the richest bar is tallest?

units.claim: Across the displayed income groups, the value does not decrease from poorest 10% to richest 10%, rising from 1.000 up to 21.000.
accept: The bars rise from the poorest group to the richest group.
Higher income groups have higher values, reaching 21 for the richest 10%.
There is no downward step in the sequence from 1 up to 21.
units.evidence: All displayed income-group bars must be visible in income order with non-decreasing heights.

units.claim: The richest 10% has a value of 21.000 versus 1.000 for the poorest 10%; this is 20.000 higher and 21 times larger.
accept: The richest 10% pay 21 while the poorest 10% pay 1.
The richest 10% are 20 points higher than the poorest 10%.
The richest 10% value is 21 times the poorest 10% value.
units.evidence: Both endpoint bars must be visible with their values or labels.

units.claim: The richest 10% is the top endpoint, with the highest displayed value 21.000 and relative_value 0.7000.
accept: The richest 10% have the highest value: 21.000.
The top group reaches a relative_value of 0.7000.
The richest bar is tallest at 21.
units.evidence: The richest 10% bar must be visibly the tallest and labeled 21.000 or 0.7000.

optional_valid: The poorest 10% is the lowest endpoint at value 1.000 and relative_value 0.0333.
The full displayed value series can be shown: 1,1,2,3,4,6,7,9,12,21.
The richest 10% relative_value 0.7000 is the maximum relative_value shown.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded
